_comment_v0_13_0: Clip ceiling raised 10.13s -> 15.08s (362 frames), the top of H3's trained range, so a scene that genuinely wants an unbroken take can have one. This does NOT change the default length: duration is still DERIVED FROM THE DIALOGUE (v0.11.0) and 5.17s remains both the efficiency optimum (27.3s of wall clock per second of video, against 42.8 at 15.08s) and the floor of H3's trained range. The old 8s/10s caps were justified by a "cost cliff" that has since been retracted as measurement noise -- see _comment_maxClipSec. Also in this version: workflows/minimax_h3_r2v.json switches the unet from pruned_nvfp4 to nvfp4_full, which measured FASTER (141s vs 169s at 124f, 334s vs 407s at 226f -- paired within one run at both lengths) as well as being the better weights; the earlier preference for pruned was reasoning from a VRAM budget that does not exist (in-flight VRAM is pinned at ~31.6 of 32 GiB at EVERY clip length, and the text encoder is already offloaded to CPU by default). Prompt and schema now also state that CUTS INSIDE A RENDER ARE FREE -- cost is frames, not cut count -- so no cut should ever be dropped to save time.
_comment_v0_12_0: Upscale pass swapped comfy.rtx_vsr -> comfy.ltx_upscale (founder directive 2026-08-04), and the merge node now pins maxClipSec 10.13 to mirror scene_clip.maxSeconds so authored timecodes match rendered clip length. The VSR->LTX swap lifts the ceiling on this bundle's cheap-render strategy: VSR only sharpened what survived a 480p render, so a soft face stayed soft; LTX's upsample+refine is generative and rebuilds it, at ~45s per 5s clip (vs ~12s per clip for VSR). Same target contract, so it was a same-node swap. NOTE on stage ordering: the founder asked that every H3 render finish before any upscaling starts, to stop the GPU swapping between the H3 and LTX weights. That is ALREADY guaranteed by dhee-core's walker with no core change -- walker.ts executes strictly node-by-node (`for (const node of ordered)`), draining every instance of a node before the next node starts, and scene_upscaled takes scene_clip as an input so topological order puts all 1..N clips before any upscale. Verified against a real run.log, where each collection's instances drain contiguously (all character_anchor_prompt items, then all object_anchor_prompt items, ...). No bundle or engine change was needed for the ordering guarantee.
_comment_v0_11_0: Clip duration is now DERIVED FROM THE DIALOGUE instead of dividing a chapter's seconds evenly across however many sections a model happened to author. MEASURED across 7 H3 renders (720p, seed 4242, Hindi, 2026-08-04): H3 generates audio from the prompt and STRETCHES OR COMPRESSES the spoken line to fill the clip -- leadInSilence + speechSpan == clipLength, every time, in all 7. Both failure modes follow from that one behaviour: a 5-word line in a 5.17s clip padded with 2.94s of DEAD AIR before she spoke, and a 9-word line in the same 5.17s clip ran to the final frame with zero tail (rushed/truncated). So clip length must MATCH the dialogue, not merely exceed it -- over-allocating is a defect too, which is why the old even division was wrong in BOTH directions regardless of section count, and why capping section count would only have picked a different accident. Natural pace measured off the longest (least padding-distorted) line: ~2.8 words/sec, plus ~1.0s fixed lead-in+tail, plus 0.35s between separate utterances. Capacity per legal grid point: 124f/5.17s ~12 words, 192f/8.0s ~20 words, 243f/10.13s ~27 words. FOUNDER POLICY (2026-08-04): short beats stay their OWN sections and the dead-air pad is ACCEPTED, preserving deliberate dramatic silences -- so the budget is only ever raised to max(evenShare, speechNeed), NEVER shrunk and NEVER merged. Implemented in plan.chapter_merge (budgetSec = snapToH3Grid(max(evenShare, speechSecondsFor(spokenLines)))) so scene_detail authors correct per-shot durations AND correct [Shot N] At MM:SS timecodes, and enforced again as a render-time FLOOR in comfy.minimax_h3_r2v's resolveSeconds so an LLM-authored duration can never squeeze the words. A beat needing more than the ceiling gets speechOverflowSec + a loud warning: it needs an upstream re-plan, not a bigger clip. ALSO in this version: the <d> dialogue tag must sit as EARLY in its shot as possible. Measured on one line and seed -- moving the tag to the front cut lead-in silence 1.33s -> 0.40s, while INSTRUCTING H3 that 'her voice begins on the very first frame' changed it by exactly 0.00s and deleting the pre-speech action changed it by -0.30s (worse). H3 renders the ORDER the prose is written in; an assertion about timing is just more prose. Position is the lever, not wording.
_comment_v0_10_0: Non-English dialogue must be authored in its language's NATIVE SCRIPT, never romanized into Latin. MEASURED via a seed-matched A/B render (1280x720, 124f, seed 4242, identical graph): the Hindi line 'Aap kya padh rahi hain? Mujhe Delhi jaana hai.' was voiced with English phonetics on exactly the tokens Latin cannot spell -- 'padh' got an English d instead of the retroflex dh, 'Delhi' came out anglicised -- while the identical line as 'आप क्या पढ़ रही हैं? मुझे दिल्ली जाना है।' was pronounced correctly throughout. H3 reads text phonetically off the script it is written in, and romanized Hindi is full of tokens that are also English-shaped (hai, main, koi, Delhi, data). The convention is enforced in FOUR places: chapter_screenplay.md (where dialogue is born, and the last cheap place to fix the script), chapter_outline.md + chapter_outline.schema.json (spokenLines, copied verbatim downstream), and scene_video_prompt.md (whose shipped <d>[Hindi] example was itself romanized -- examples teach harder than rules, so that example WAS the bug). Backed structurally by auditDialogueScript() in dhee-runner-minimax-h3, which fails a render whose <d>[Language] tag names a non-Latin-script language but whose words contain none of that script; the test is 'at least one native character', so a Hindi line embedding Latin proper nouns stays legal.
displayName: Illustrated Story · MiniMax H3 Film (any-length chapters, multi-cut scenes, stateful characters)
summary: Turns a story of ANY LENGTH into a directed film with native synced stereo audio. Identical planning to illustrated_story_msr -- any-length chapter split, per-chapter bible/screenplay/outline with previousN carry-forward, canonical anchor plates for every recurring character, story-critical object and location, and a character STATE ledger with per-state edited plates -- but the film is no longer assembled from one-shot clips. Each SECTION is rendered as ONE MiniMax H3 (Hailuo 03) reference-to-video generation of up to 15 seconds containing SEVERAL CUTS, directed by a timecoded shot list, with the camera moves, the transitions between cuts and the whole sound design authored in the same prompt. Up to 9 reference plates per scene, each given an explicit job.
techLine: ANY-LENGTH CHAPTER SPLIT · PER-CHAPTER SCREENPLAY/BIBLE/OUTLINE (previousN carry-forward) · DETERMINISTIC MERGE · CHARACTER/OBJECT/LOCATION ANCHOR PLATES · CHARACTER STATE LEDGER · PER-STATE EDITED PLATES · MINIMAX H3 MULTI-CUT REFERENCE-TO-VIDEO SCENES (up to 15s, native stereo AV, 9 refs) · FINAL CUT
description:
The MiniMax H3 sibling of illustrated_story_msr. Everything up to and including the character-state plates is byte-for-byte the same pipeline; what changes is the last stretch of the graph.

illustrated_story_msr renders one LTX MSR clip per SHOT (4-10s, one continuous take, no cuts) and concatenates them, so every cut in the finished film is a boundary between two independent generations. H3 inverts that: it renders 5-15 seconds containing SEVERAL CUTS in a single pass, so a whole scene -- its coverage, its whip pans, its hard cuts on impact, its ambient bed and foley and dialogue -- comes out of one generation, internally consistent by construction. So the per-shot nodes (shot_brief, shot_video_prompt, shot_clip) are replaced by two per-SECTION nodes: scene_video_prompt authors a timecoded multi-cut shot list for one section, and scene_clip renders it. The existing planner already budgets sections at roughly 15 seconds each (plan.chapter_merge splits a chapter's durationSec across its sections), so one section maps cleanly onto one H3 call, and the section's planned shots become the CUTS INSIDE that call rather than separate clips.

The prompt stage encodes MiniMax's own documented H3 guidance: every reference is given an explicit job (the single highest-leverage instruction for this model), the shot list is timecoded so a 15s render does not drift into a slideshow, transitions are described as physical events rather than named effects, the audio is directed as deliberately as the picture, and the negatives live in the prompt prose -- because the H3 ref2va graph is guidance-distilled and has no negative conditioning input at all. The '<Picture N>' reference-binding clause is NOT written by the authoring model (it cannot know the final slot order); the runner builds it deterministically from each reference's appearsAs + job after state substitution and background-last routing have run.

inputs.label: Story
inputs.placeholder: Paste a story of ANY length — a short story or a full novel. It becomes a narrated animated film, chaptered and paced off its own length.

inputs.default: cinematic photoreal — filmic lighting, shallow depth of field, natural colour grade
inputs.label: Visual style hint
inputs.placeholder: A hint the art-style step builds on. Leave as-is for cinematic photoreal.

inputs.label: Narrator voiceover

options.label: Yes — a designed narrator voices narration beats

inputs.placeholder: false (default) = a pure movie: characters speak natively in-scene, non-dialogue beats play on action + ambient sound. true = a designed narrator voices narration-mode beats.

inputs.label: Target length (seconds)
inputs.placeholder: "auto" (default) DERIVES the film's length from the story's own length (see the rate below) — no fixed ceiling, a longer story yields a longer film. Or type an explicit number of seconds (e.g. 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, or any longer figure) to force a fixed length instead.

inputs.label: Auto-length rate (seconds per 1000 words) — describes the pacing this pass actually authors, not a budget it is forced into
inputs.placeholder: Only used when Target length is "auto". Seconds of finished film per 1000 words of story prose — 180 (default, v0.9.0) means a 6,000-word story runs ~18 minutes and a 90,000-word novel runs ~4.5 hours. `target_duration` is DESCRIPTIVE of the authoring pass's natural pacing, not a CAP it is compressed into.
inputs._comment: v0.9.0: recalibrated 60 → 180 (founder decision, dheeai/dhee-runner-story-chapters#4). 60 was never derived from what this pass actually authors -- it was a guess. Real authored output across three runs of this exact bundle measured 120-229s of finished film per 1000 words (lamp_keeper_msr: 899w → 108s = 120s/1000w; lamp_keeper_v2: 1591w → 364s = 229s/1000w; lamp_keeper_v3: 1591w → 285.4s = 179s/1000w), landing near 180s/1000w in aggregate, while budgetSec injection into scene_detail was independently confirmed exact (scene_outline summed to the OLD 60s/1000w target to the decimal) -- so the overshoot was never a budgetSec-arithmetic bug, and it was consistent across BOTH the deepseek run (2.0x over the old target) and the g4 runs (3.0-3.8x over it), so it was never a model-quality problem either. The founder's call: stop trying to compress an LLM authoring pass's natural pacing down to an arbitrary rate by discarding shots it already wrote: raise the rate to match reality instead. Consequence, stated plainly: films now come out roughly 3x longer than under the old default -- a 90,000-word novel derives ~4.5 hours of target film rather than ~1.5 hours. This is deliberate. plan.assemble_keyframes' own duration-budget tripwire (chaptersInput, unchanged, still ±25% durationTolerance -- do NOT loosen it, it is now a genuinely useful signal) still catches any run whose ACTUAL authored pacing strays from whatever rate is configured; it is not being silenced by this change, only recalibrated against a truer baseline.

inputs.label: Render resolution
inputs.placeholder: 'native' (1344x768) is H3's own geometry and the best quality. Cost scales as ~pixels^1.3, so '480p' (832x480) renders ~3.7x faster -- use it to iterate on a story, then re-render the final cut at native. Accepts an explicit '<w>x<h>' too.

inputs.label: Location photo (optional)
inputs.description: A real photograph of the primary location. Supply it and it replaces the generated location plate on every clip. Only ONE background plate survives per clip (H3 treats extra backgrounds as clutter), so this displaces the generated one rather than adding to it.

inputs.label: Sampler steps
inputs.placeholder: 'auto' (default) scales 4/6/8/10 with scene complexity — cuts, references, dialogue lines and duration. A number pins every scene to that count. 4 is the turbo LoRA's distilled step count; above ~10 costs time without a measured gain.

inputs.label: Character photo 1 (optional)
inputs.placeholder: A real face. Name them below and this photo is used instead of an invented one — no plate is generated.

inputs.label: Who is character photo 1?
inputs.placeholder: The name the story uses, e.g. Meera

inputs.label: Character photo 2 (optional)
inputs.placeholder: A real face. Name them below and this photo is used instead of an invented one — no plate is generated.

inputs.label: Who is character photo 2?
inputs.placeholder: The name the story uses, e.g. Meera

inputs.label: Character photo 3 (optional)
inputs.placeholder: A real face. Name them below and this photo is used instead of an invented one — no plate is generated.

inputs.label: Who is character photo 3?
inputs.placeholder: The name the story uses, e.g. Meera

config._comment_v0_28_0_write_out_length: v0.28.0 The premise write-out now knows how long the film is. plan.story_prepare only ever interpolated {{story_input}}, and prompts/story.md told it to 'let the story's own shape decide its length' -- so a 15-second film and a ten-minute film got byte-identical instructions. Measured: a 98-word premise for a 15s film came back at 758 words, roughly 9x the ~83 words that 15s buys at 180s/1000 words. Everything downstream then compresses or truncates it. The runner (>=0.7.0) derives a word budget from these two inputs and hands the write-out a hard range; when target_duration is 'auto' there is no budget and the open-ended instruction stands, which is right -- 'auto' means the story's length decides the film's, not the other way round.

nodes.displayName: Chapter Bible (per-chapter visual identity, carried forward)

config._comment: v0.3.0: the 'chapter_bible' self-edge above (scope:previousN, n:1) is dhee-core's generalized previousN ordering. Exposes ctx.inputs.chapter_bible as an ordered array (newest-first; with n:1 just the immediately-preceding chapter) of { shotNumber, itemId, outputAbs, content } — content is the FULL prior chapter's bible JSON, inlined since this node's output format is json. Empty array for the very first chapter (ch_01). The prompt (prompts/chapter_bible.md) re-emits any carried-forward entity with its EXACT same id and description copied verbatim — the downstream plan.chapter_merge (mode:bible) union keeps the FIRST definition of every id across the whole film and silently drops later duplicates, so a drifted re-description here is simply lost, never an improvement. concurrency is explicitly 1 for readers — the engine already force-clamps any node with a previousN input to serial regardless of this value, since chapter N+1's call depends on chapter N's own completed bible output.

nodes.displayName: Story Bible (visual identity, merged across chapters)

config._comment_v0_19_0_schema: Schema added after a silent identity failure on a real film: the LIRA pass returned the art style's suffix line and nothing else for one character (202 chars, no character in it), nothing rejected it, and H3 got crops of an empty style frame as her identity reference in every scene. The node had no outputSchema at all. object_anchor_prompt and location_anchor_prompt are still unschema'd and carry the same risk -- their contracts differ (single view, not a four-view sheet) so they need their own.

config._comment_v0_21_0_plate_res: v0.21.0 REFERENCE PLATE RESOLUTION. Measured on a real film: H3 was being handed 384x864 plates to render a 1344x768 frame. The 1536x864 sheet was split into FOUR 384px-wide panels, which puts a full-body face at ~60-80px -- below the resolution at which 'one obsidian eye', 'copper wire in grey hair' or 'seams in cooled lava' exist at all, let alone transfer. The bundle already makes this argument for the OUTPUT (it renders native because 480p 'resolves the face to too few pixels'); it was never applied to the INPUT. TWO of the four panels were also pure waste: scene_clip has always used sheetPick [0, 3] with viewsPerCharacter 2, so the profile and back views were generated, stored, state-edited, joined and then discarded. So the sheet is now TWO panels -- the full-body front and the medium close-up, exactly the two that were used -- at 2048x1152 instead of 1536x864. Each panel goes 384x864 -> 1024x1152: 2.7x linear, 3.5x the pixels on the character, for ~1.8x the generation cost and TWO fewer state edits per character rather than more. The sheet is kept rather than generating separate plates because one generation is what guarantees the same person across views; separate calls do not. refImageSize also moves 'match' -> 'max' so H3 keeps up to 2048px short edge instead of downscaling the new detail straight back to the render size.
config._comment_v0_26_0_cast_photos: v0.26.0 CAST PHOTOS. Three optional slots let an operator hand the film a REAL face for a character, each paired with a name field. comfy.tti (dhee-runner-image-edit >=0.8.0) matches the typed name against this item's id by token containment -- 'Ramesh' and 'Ramesh Kulkarni' both bind to ramesh_kulkarni, 'Nisha' does not -- and on a match COPIES the photo to this node's output without calling Comfy at all. The plate is SKIPPED, not generated and then displaced. This supersedes protagonist_photo for the character case: that input is a pinnedRef on scene_clip, which attaches one face to every clip and still pays to generate the plate it displaces. It is kept for back-compat and for the single-lead shorthand. KNOWN DIFFERENCE: a generated plate is a TWO-VIEW sheet that scene_clip splits into #v0/#v1, so a character gets two reference slots. A supplied photograph is one view and yields ONE slot. That is usually the right trade for a real face, but it is a real behavioural difference and not a bug. Matching is deliberately strict: a near miss falls through to generation rather than binding the wrong face to a character.

config._comment: v0.3.0: the 'chapter_screenplay' self-edge above (scope:previousN, n:1) is dhee-core's generalized previousN ordering. Exposes ctx.inputs.chapter_screenplay as an ordered array (newest-first; with n:1 just the immediately-preceding chapter) of { shotNumber, itemId, outputAbs, content } — content is the FULL prior chapter's screenplay markdown, inlined since this node's output format is markdown. Empty array for the very first chapter (ch_01). The prompt (prompts/chapter_screenplay.md) uses it ONLY for continuity (where characters physically are, what they wear/carry, what just happened, the emotional temperature) and must NOT re-stage or recap anything it already covered. concurrency is explicitly 1 for readers — the engine already force-clamps any node with a previousN input to serial regardless of this value, since chapter N+1's call depends on chapter N's own completed screenplay output.
config._comment_draft: v0.16.0: this is the DIRECTOR'S DRAFT. It keeps prompts/chapter_screenplay.md and all of the adaptation authoring; the node id moved so that `chapter_screenplay` can become the REVIEWED output. Doing it this way means every downstream consumer (director_screenplay, chapter_outline, chapter_state) and every {{chapter_screenplay}} template variable keeps working untouched -- llm.generate derives template vars from input IDs, so repointing consumers instead would have silently broken two prompts. KNOWN LIMITATION: the previousN continuity carry-forward reads the previous chapter's DRAFT, not its reviewed version, because chapter_screenplay depends on this node and reading it back would be a node-level cycle. That is safe only because the reviewer is forbidden from adding, deleting, reordering or rewriting BEATS -- so the events continuity depends on are identical in both.

config._comment:
v0.16.0 COVERAGE CRITIC. Closes the loop that the v0.15.0 Adaptation table opened. The table is supposed to hold one row per meaningful element of the chapter, each with a disposition saying HOW it reaches the audience; an element with NO row is the chapter's meaning going missing invisibly, and a single forward authoring pass cannot catch its own omissions. This pass re-reads the SOURCE PROSE against the table -- in that direction, because reading the draft and asking 'does this look complete' always says yes.

It is deliberately a REVISE pass, not a report. A critic whose output nothing consumes is a file nobody reads, so this one emits the corrected screenplay and takes over the `chapter_screenplay` node id -- downstream is unchanged and cannot skip it.

Its mandate is narrow and its default is NO CHANGE: it may only fix the five named defects (unaccounted element, interiority marked DRAMATISE, a disposition that lands in no beat, an unjustified CUT, broken table<->beat correspondence), and it MUST NOT add, delete, reorder or rewrite beats -- only add a line/prop/sound to an existing beat so a disposition lands. That constraint is what keeps the draft-based previousN continuity valid, and it is why this is not just a second author. A clean draft is output verbatim.

Appends a `### Coverage Audit` section recording what was found and changed, so the pass is auditable rather than a silent rewrite -- the same principle as the disposition table itself.

Sequencing note: this was built AFTER the disposition table on purpose. bundles_removed_no_direction_planning/ holds two agentic bundles that were pulled for lacking direction planning; a critic with no concrete artifact to check against has nothing to do but re-author. The table is that artifact.

nodes.displayName: Director Screenplay (plain-English source of truth, merged across chapters)
Scene Outline (title + section skeletons, merged + globally renumbered)

config._comment_maxClipSec: v0.13.0: 15.09, mirroring scene_clip.maxSeconds 15 so the budget a section is authored against equals the clip length actually rendered -- otherwise the [Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm cut times land out of sync with the finished clip. Why 15.09 and not 15.08: resolveClipCeilingSec snaps a configured value DOWN to a legal grid point, and 15.08*24 = 361.92 would fall to 345f (14.375s), surrendering 0.71s. 15.09*24 = 362.16 snaps down to 362f = 15.083s, which is what scene_clip renders (the h3 runner snaps UP, so maxSeconds 15 -> 360f -> 362f). CORRECTS TWO CLAIMS in the v0.12.0 version of this comment. (a) It said "H3's absolute maximum is 10.83s (260f)" -- wrong; the node tooltip gives the trained range as ~124-362 frames, i.e. up to 15.08s, and 362f has been rendered successfully. (b) It said "226f+ costs ~3.5x marginal", citing a cost cliff that is now RETRACTED: re-measured with fixed steps, 192f->226f came out 306->491s where the original sweep read 288->573s, and the box shows 10-21% run-to-run variance on byte-identical configs, so the "cliff" was noise. Historical cost (720p, 20 steps, then-active graph): 124f 141s, 226f 334s, 362f ~645s with the then-active cache recipe -- roughly frames^1.4, smooth, no discontinuity. A 15s take costs ~1.7x per second of video versus a 5.17s one, which is a premium worth paying for a scene that wants an unbroken take rather than a reason to cap. See dhee-cofounder/memory/2026-08-04-h3-cost-scales-as-frames-1-42.md and artifacts/h3-r2v-probe/README.md.
config._comment: v0.8.0: plan.chapter_merge (mode:sections) >=0.3.0 now ALSO injects a deterministic per-section budgetSec/targetShotCount — that section's own chapter's durationSec split evenly across however many sections that chapter's chapter_outline pass actually produced. This is the fix for a real regression: films were coming out 2-4x their target length (lamp_keeper_msr 108s vs a 54s target, lamp_keeper_v2 364s vs a 95s target) because the LLM-authored pacing guidance in prompts/chapter_outline.md (sections ≈ durationSec ÷ 15) and prompts/scene_detail.md's own duration arithmetic were both prose the model did not reliably follow. Doing the division here — deterministically, after the section count is already fixed — makes the film's TOTAL duration correct BY CONSTRUCTION regardless of how many sections the outline pass created. This is a PROPORTIONAL BUDGET, never a cap — it scales without limit with durationSec and section count. Do NOT delete this under the belief it re-introduces a section-count ceiling; it does not. See prompts/scene_detail.md (consumes budgetSec/targetShotCount directly) and plan.assemble_keyframes' chaptersInput tripwire (scenes_plan node below) which verifies the fix held.
config._comment_pacing_derives_from_clip_cap: v0.8.1: secondsPerShot 8 (the default) -> 4, so that ONE number governs pacing everywhere. A SECTION is exactly one H3 clip and scene_clip caps a clip at 8s (measured: H3's marginal cost jumps ~3.5x between 8.00s and 9.42s). chapter_outline therefore splits at durationSec/8, budgetSec lands ~8, and targetShotCount = round(8/4) = 2 shots of ~4s as CUTS INSIDE that one clip. Previously the outline split at durationSec/15 while the clip capped at 8, so every section was budgeted ~15s and silently lost ~47% of its beats to the clamp -- a 35-section film came out 4m34s against a 6m34s plan. It also created an UNSATISFIABLE DEAD ZONE: with secondsPerShot 8, any budgetSec in (10,12] gave targetShotCount 1 while a shot's schema maximum was 10, so no valid output existed and the run died after three attempts (issue #2). With secondsPerShot 4 and a shot maximum of 8 the dead zone is gone for every budgetSec >= 2. [CORRECTED v0.13.0: the '~3.5x marginal cost jump between 8.00s and 9.42s' cited here is RETRACTED as measurement noise -- re-measured with fixed steps, 192f->226f came out 306->491s against the original sweep's 288->573s, on a box showing 10-21% run-to-run variance. Real cost is a smooth ~frames^1.4. The clip ceiling is now 15.08s (362f); the pacing divisor deliberately stays UNDER it at 8 so sections default short and only speech-heavy ones grow. The historical reasoning below is kept because the REGRESSIONS it describes were real.]

config._comment: v0.5.0 — director_screenplay REMOVED from this node's inputs. Root cause of duplicated scenes/dialogue in long films (bundle issue: repeated beats): this pass used to receive the WHOLE whole-film screenplay as context and had to work out which lines were its own. It cannot be done reliably. Measured on hunt2 (134 sections, illustrated_story_msr, plan authored 2026-08-03 AFTER the prose scope-fence landed 2026-08-01): 13 dialogue lines duplicated across sections, including a whole 3-shot block staged in BOTH scene_13 and scene_14, whose briefs were distinct ('offers an audition' vs 'invites her to the bungalow') — so the fence was obeyed and the film still played the beat twice. The screenplay is organised into 31 named beat blocks with ZERO scene_N markers, while the outline has 134 sections whose headings ('The Bait', 'The Invitation') appear NOWHERE in it; scene_12-16 all fall inside one undivided '**The Change**' block holding both scene_13's line (screenplay line 108) and scene_14's (line 116). Nothing in the inputs assigned line 108 to one rather than the other — the duplication was UNDERDETERMINED BY CONSTRUCTION, not a discipline failure, which is why a prose fence could never fix it. Duplication tracked the sections:screenplay-blocks ratio across the corpus (4:1 -> 13 dupes, 2.4:1 -> 11, 1.2:1 -> 3, 1:1 -> 0). FIX: chapter_outline is the one node that holds a SINGLE chapter's screenplay AND decides where that chapter's section boundaries fall, so it alone knows which lines land in which beat — it now records them per section on `spokenLines` (it was already reading them to set `mode`, then discarding them). plan.chapter_merge needed NO change: chapterMerge.ts spreads `{...s}` so the field reaches scene_outline for free (both schemas gained the field; scene_outline.schema.json has additionalProperties:false and would otherwise fail the merge). scene_detail reads its dialogue from its OWN section's spokenLines, which it already locates by item_id. Also drops context from ~144KB to ~12KB per call (~92% of it was other sections' material) — ~4.8M -> ~450K tokens on a 134-section film. director_screenplay the NODE stays: scenes_plan still needs it for plan.assemble_keyframes' dialogue recovery.
config._comment_spokenlines_one_shot: v0.5.2 fixes a bug INTRODUCED by v0.5.0's own prompt. The spokenLines instruction read 'One entry per shot, in order', which the model read as 'every shot gets an entry'. With ONE line and TWO shots it put the SAME line on both, so the finished film would speak it twice in a row -- trading the old cross-SECTION duplication for a new within-SECTION one. Measured on unseeing_role (35 sections): 6 repeated dialogue values, and 5 of the 6 were a single line duplicated across two shots of the SAME section (scene_13/23/28/5/2), caught at the plan checkpoint before any clip rendered. The prompt now states that each entry appears in EXACTLY ONE shot, that shots outnumbering lines are WORDLESS (no dialogue, no speaker), and that shot count and line count are independent -- extra shots are not slots to fill. A terminal check asks the model to list its own dialogue values and delete any line appearing twice. Note what the same run proved about v0.5.0 itself: of 21 lines across 35 sections and 2 chapters, only two were assigned to more than one section -- 'Ira Kulkarni.' (13 chars) and 'Thank you.' (10 chars), both genuinely repeated in the source story -- while every substantive line (255, 78, 64, 45, 27 chars) had exactly one owner. hunt2 pre-fix had 13 duplicated lines including 90+ char speeches. Cross-section leakage is fixed; this was a separate, self-inflicted regression on top of it.
config._comment_states_before_shots: v0.8.0: character_state is now an INPUT here, which is the point of inverting the chain -- shots are authored KNOWING each character's appearance at that scene, instead of appearance being annotated onto shots that already exist. DELIBERATELY still NOT given director_screenplay: v0.5.0 removed it because feeding the whole whole-film screenplay to this per-section pass is what caused cross-section dialogue duplication (13 lines duplicated on a 35-section film, one in four scenes). The screenplay still reaches shots -- via chapter_outline, which reads its own chapter's screenplay and records spokenLines per section -- so 'screenplay broken down to shots' holds through the outline rather than by handing every section the whole script again.

config._comment: v0.8.0: chaptersInput (plan.assemble_keyframes >=0.6.0) wires this node's new opt-in duration-budget TRIPWIRE — every assembled shot's duration is summed and logged against chapters.targetDurationSec ('shot budget: Xs planned vs Ys target (Z%)'), and a deviation beyond ±25% (durationTolerance, default) is recorded as a duration_budget_deviation entry in assembly_warnings.json. This NEVER fails the run and NEVER rescales durations — the real fix is upstream (scene_outline's plan.chapter_merge budgetSec/targetShotCount, see that node's _comment); this is only the tripwire proving it worked. Added after real runs (lamp_keeper_msr, lamp_keeper_v2) overshot their target 2-4x with no visibility into it.

nodes.displayName: Chapter Character Appearance State (per-chapter ledger, carried forward)

config._comment: v0.4.0: the 'chapter_state' self-edge above (scope:previousN, n:1) is dhee-core's generalized previousN ordering, the same pattern as chapter_bible/chapter_screenplay. Exposes ctx.inputs.chapter_state as an ordered array (newest-first; with n:1 just the immediately-preceding chapter) of { shotNumber, itemId, outputAbs, content } — content is the FULL prior chapter's ledger JSON, inlined since this node's output format is json. Empty array for the very first chapter (ch_01), whose characters instead start from the story_bible baseline. The prompt (prompts/chapter_state.md) folds each character's appearance FORWARD from the previous chapter's ending state — a signature like 'rip__bearded_rusty_gun' must be reused verbatim by every later chapter, never reinvented. This node exists because the OLD whole-film character_state (one llm.generate call emitting one ledger entry per shot per character, repeating each character's full ~800-char appearance verbatim every entry) could not fit a real novel's shot count in any fixed maxTokens — splitting per-chapter, mirroring chapter_bible/chapter_screenplay, is the fix; plan.chapter_merge (mode:states) folds the per-chapter ledgers back into the one whole-film plans/character_state.json downstream nodes already expect. concurrency is explicitly 1 for readers — the engine already force-clamps any node with a previousN input to serial regardless of this value, since chapter N+1's call depends on chapter N's own completed ledger output.
config._comment_timeline_inversion: v0.8.0 INVERTS this node. It used to consume chapter_shots and emit an exhaustive PER-SHOT ledger -- one row per shot restating every present character's full appearance. That made states DERIVED FROM shots, so a shot could never have been authored against a known state, and the schema's own demand ('every shot must appear') is documented as unenforceable in dhee-runner-story-chapters/shotBrief.ts: 'found unenforceable across three consecutive runs', with a skipped shot silently falling back to its base anchor. On a 326-shot film that is hundreds of near-identical rows and one omission corrupts a clip. It now reads the SCREENPLAY (where changes of clothes actually happen) plus the OUTLINE (for the scene ids to anchor to) and emits an ordered TIMELINE per character: {signature, appearance, from:'scene_12', change}. plan.character_states forward-fills that onto every shot deterministically, so the model writes ~2-4 rows per character instead of ~326 and the per-shot assignment is arithmetic. Locations use the identical shape for genuine look changes (day->night, a wrecked room). chapter_shots is DELETED -- chapter_state was its only consumer. The materiality bar (only CLOTHING or PHYSIQUE mints a new signature) is preserved verbatim; it is hard-won -- a real run minted 12 states where 4 were material.
config._comment_maxtokens_20k: v0.8.3: maxTokens=20000 on EVERY llm.generate node. Three nodes (the *_anchor_prompt trio) had NO maxTokens at all, and on a reasoning model that is unbounded thinking: measured on deepseek-v4-flash-0731 they cost 348s + 178s + 23s = 549s of a 1580s authoring phase (35%) to produce three short text prompts. chapter_state itself took 302s at maxTokens 12000. An explicit ceiling everywhere makes the cost bounded and the failure mode visible (a truncation error) rather than a silent multi-minute stall. Note the ceiling matters much less on LOCAL models, where dhee-core's chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking:false actually takes effect -- it is a no-op on OpenRouter, which is why the remote run was so slow.

nodes.displayName: Character Appearance State (ledger, merged across chapters)

config._comment_timeline_merge: v0.8.2 BUGFIX. v0.8.0 changed chapter_state to emit a TIMELINE (characters[]/locations[]) but left this merge still concatenating the old shots[] array, so it produced 0 shots and died on '/shots must NOT have fewer than 1 items' -- the producer's shape was changed without following the pipe. mode:'states' now selects by the ledger's SHAPE and merges timelines when it sees characters[]/locations[]. sectionsPartsInput is REQUIRED for correctness, not convenience: chapter_outline numbers sections CHAPTER-LOCALLY (scene_1..scene_N restarting each chapter) while mergeSections renumbers them globally, so a timeline's from:'scene_9' means the 9th section OF THAT CHAPTER. The merge needs each chapter's section count to shift it to the global id. Without it every `from` after chapter 1 points at the wrong scene -- invisible on a single-chapter film and silently wrong on every longer one, which is exactly the class of mistake this rework exists to remove.

config._comment_forward_fill: v0.8.0: shotsInput=scenes_plan added because the ledger is now a TIMELINE, not a per-shot table. plan.character_states selects its mode from the ledger's SHAPE -- characters[].states[] triggers forward-fill, shots[] uses the legacy transcription -- and forward-fill needs the ordered shot list to assign states onto. Output shape is unchanged ({states, byShot, baseByCharacter}), so every consumer (comfy.minimax_h3_r2v, image.sheet_split) keeps working.

config._comment: v0.10.0: prompts/character_state_prompt.md rewritten around the NEXT-LAYER rule — when a garment comes off, describe the most natural next layer INWARD for this character (one step only), decided by garment type, sex, period, region, station and climate: a man's shirt off reveals his bare chest; a woman's top off reveals her period-appropriate breast covering (bra / chemise / choli); trousers or a skirt off reveal that period's lower undergarment and almost never bare skin; gloves/boots/hat have no intermediate layer. Multi-layer costume (Victorian, winter, ceremonial) steps inward ONCE, never collapsing to skin. Validated in dhee-cofounder/artifacts/state-edit-reveal-bakeoff/FINDINGS.md — read it before editing this prompt. TWO TRAPS documented there: (1) NEVER quote a bad output inside this prompt even as a warning — four separate authoring models reproduced verbatim every failure phrase and every worked-example garment the prompt named, which is why this file now contains no example garment descriptions at all; (2) the old rule mandating a negative clause ('...with no trousers') was itself what produced the bare-legs failure — the negative clause must attach to the REVEALED LAYER and deny only the one garment that came off. tier 'heavy' should resolve to thinkingcap-27b OR qwen-27b — both score 4/4 fully clean on the four validation states, re-measured against THIS version of the prompt. qwen-35b scores 2/4 (it describes a bare torso where a woman's top comes off instead of her breast covering, and writes 'trousers are removed', a banned diff word) — the SMALLER qwen is the better author here, so do not assume parameter count tracks quality on this task. g4-meromero is unusable: incoherent output, and it returns EMPTY content unless chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false is set, because it spends the entire token budget in reasoning_content on a prompt this long (reasoning_budget:0 is silently ignored by the gateway; '/no_think' only half works). Every model tested improved once the prompt's example garment descriptions were purged, which is the strongest evidence for trap (1).

nodes.displayName: Character State View Plan (per-view tile crop + prompt assembly)

config._comment: v0.6.0: replaces the old single-call comfy.image_edit whole-sheet edit. Measured (dhee-cofounder/artifacts/krea-sheet-state-edit-probe/FINDINGS.md) to fail two independent ways: denoise 1.0 from an EMPTY latent re-imagines the sheet instead of editing it (layout collapses), and even once that is fixed, one instruction cannot bind to N repeated sheet instances (a change lands on some views, not all). The fix is PER-VIEW tile edits expressed as a REAL DAG fan-out (12 states x 4 views = 48 comfy.image_edit calls) rather than hidden inside one runner -- a collection cannot fan N-per-item off another collection, so this STAGE crops+upscales each state's base sheet into its 4 view tiles and assembles each view's edit prompt (identity-only text from character_state_prompt + the fixed per-view clause below + the hard studio constraint) into one flat plan.views[] array; character_state_view_tile/character_state_view_prompt then fan 48 real per-item instances off that array (a stage's own scope:'matching' input can't itself expose one filtered entry to a downstream node -- same reason dhee-runner-video-split/dhee-runner-audio-split exist), and comfy.image_edit + workflows/krea2_edit.json are consumed completely UNCHANGED, genuinely 1:1 (one tile in, one edited tile out). denoise stays krea2_edit.json's own default (1.0) -- FINDINGS round 4 found 1.0 with a clean identity-only instruction handles additive, subtractive AND full-replacement deltas uniformly, so no override is wired here.
viewClauses: This is the full-body view of the character standing and facing the camera directly; keep that exact framing and camera angle.
This is the medium close-up view of the character, head to waist, facing the camera; keep that exact framing and crop.
config.studioConstraint: The character is photographed in a plain neutral studio against a plain neutral seamless backdrop, with soft even neutral studio lighting and no environment, no ground texture, no cast shadows, no outdoor location and no scene whatsoever. Do not change the backdrop, the lighting or the framing of this photograph.
config._comment_v0_21_0: Two views, matching the two the renderer has always actually used. Halves the state-edit work per character.

nodes.displayName: Character State View Tiles (per-view crop, 4 per state)
Character State View Prompts (per-view edit instruction, 4 per state)
Character State View Edits (krea2 identity edit, per view tile)

config._comment: v0.6.0: comfy.image_edit and workflows/krea2_edit.json are UNMODIFIED and used exactly as any other single-image identity edit -- this node is genuinely 1:1 (one view tile in, one edited tile out), 48 instances (12 states x 4 views), fed by character_state_view_tile (the reference image, routed via referenceInputs) and character_state_view_prompt (the pre-assembled per-view prompt). width/height are the deterministic long-edge-1024-snapped-to-16 upscale of this bundle's fixed 384x864 tile size (a 1536x864 4-view anchor sheet always yields exact 384x864 panels) -- see dhee-runner-sheet-tiles' geometry.upscaleLongEdge.

v0.6.0: replaces the single comfy.image_edit whole-sheet call. Downscales this state's 4 edited view tiles (character_state_view) back to their original panel boxes and pastes them into a fresh canvas of the base anchor sheet's own dimensions -- deterministic recomposite, no model call. Errors rather than silently compositing if fewer than 4 edited tiles resolve, and errors if the composite comes out pixel-identical to the base sheet (a transient upstream failure must never read as a real, if boring, result -- see FINDINGS.md's 'Probe hygiene note'). Output pattern UNCHANGED from the prior single-call version so shot_clip needs no change.

nodes.displayName: Scene Video Prompt (H3-ready: timecoded multi-cut shot list + reference jobs + audio)

config._comment: Iterates SECTIONS, not shots -- that is the whole H3 change. The section's planned shots (visible in scenes_plan) become the CUTS inside one render, and their summed duration is the section's budget, clamped to H3's 5-15s window by the renderer. scenes_plan is wired WITHOUT scope:'matching' on purpose: it is a STAGE with one instance, so the whole plan arrives and the template locates this call's section by {{item_id}} -- exactly how scene_detail already reads scene_outline. The template must never emit a slot number ('Image 1'/'Picture 2'): comfy.minimax_h3_r2v prepends its own <Picture N> binding clause built from references[].appearsAs + references[].job, after state substitution and background-last routing, and a second contradictory numbering breaks identity. maxTokens LOWERED 20000 -> 6000 (2026-08-03). At 20000 g4-meromero ran away and emitted a ~21KB string that was truncated mid-token into unterminated JSON; llm.generate's retry then appended that 21KB draft as an assistant message, pushing the request to 47028 tokens against g4-meromero's 32768 context, and the recoverable parse error became a hard 400. The whole JSON for this node is ~4-5KB, so 6000 is generous and caps the runaway. NOTE the conversational retry is only free when the failed draft fits the remaining context -- on a modest-context local model a large runaway poisons its own retry, so keep maxTokens close to the real output size rather than at the model ceiling.
config._comment_own_shots_only: v0.5.3: this node leaks NEIGHBOURS' DIALOGUE, a separate instance of the duplication bug from the scene_detail one fixed in v0.5.0. It receives the WHOLE scenes_plan (every section's shots) and must take only the shots prefixed with its own section id. Measured on unseeing_role (35 sections, qwen-35b): 13 lines appeared in the RENDERED detailedDescription prose of more than one scene -- a 78-char line staged in FOUR scenes (9/19/20/21), a 45-char line in two -- so the finished film would have spoken them repeatedly. Caught before any clip rendered. Crucially this is NOT the underdetermined case scene_detail had: every shot in the plan is explicitly tagged with its owning section (scene_20_shot_1), so the correct answer is unambiguous and the model was simply not filtering. The prompt now states the `<section id>_shot_` prefix as the exact and only test, names the measured 4-scene failure, and adds terminal check 0b: list every <d> and delete any line that is not in your own shots. Also fixes spokenLines being authored WITH the markup ('<d>[English] Thank you.</d>' instead of 'Thank you.'). Model note: scene authoring moved from g4-meromero-192k to qwen-35b for this run because g4 collapsed into a repetition loop on two sections -- it appended a subject_definitions block (which the RUNNER writes) and ran 'and <Subject 4> and <Subject 5>...' out to <Subject 695> until maxTokens 6000 truncated it mid-string, failing all 3 attempts and killing the run. scene_video_prompt.md now caps subject numbers at the reference count and forbids appending definitions.
config._comment_concurrency: concurrency 2 -> 5 (v0.5.4), from a measured breakdown of the 34s-per-scene authoring cost on qwen-35b. The box is NOT slow: free generation measured 200-300 tok/s warm and prefill of the 15,219-token scenes_plan ran at ~5,073 tok/s (3s). Thinking is already disabled by dhee-core (LLMClient.ts sends chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false). So of 34s per scene, ~3s is prefill and free-decoding ~1,400 output tokens would be ~6s -- the remaining ~25s is GBNF grammar-constrained decoding, an effective ~47 tok/s against 250 free, i.e. a ~5x penalty. llama.cpp evaluates the grammar stack per token on the CPU, so the GPU sits largely idle through it and extra concurrent slots are close to free. Two things drive the token count and therefore the penalty: detailedDescription.minLength 1940 (forces ~500 words, deliberately, per the MiniMax H3 guide's 350-500 range) and the nested references/enum schema. Lowering minLength would cut wall-clock proportionally but costs prompt quality, so raise parallelism first. Cautionary note on measuring this: a first attempt reported 3.6 tok/s and blamed VRAM contention -- it was rotating FOUR different models in one loop, so every call paid a ~27s cold model load (qwen-35b measured). Always warm the model and hold it fixed before timing anything on this gateway.
config._comment_duration_one_number: v0.5.5 collapses THREE independent duration numbers into one. They were: scene_video_prompt.schema.json duration maximum 15, the scene_clip runner's maxSeconds 8, and chapter_outline's `sections = durationSec/15` pacing divisor. That mismatch cost a schema-validation retry on roughly one prompt in eight and then KILLED a 35-section run when scene_27 failed '/duration must be <= 15' three times. The schema maximum is now 8 and both the prompt header ('up to 8 seconds here') and step 4 ('clamped to 5-8 seconds - 8 is the hard ceiling, not 15') agree with it. After the change scene_27 authored on the first attempt. The pacing divisor is still 15 and still disagrees -- see issue #2; sections therefore get budgeted ~11s and each scene prompt clamps down to 8, dropping its least essential beat by design rather than by accident. [CORRECTED v0.13.0: the '~3.5x marginal cost jump between 8.00s and 9.42s' cited here is RETRACTED as measurement noise -- re-measured with fixed steps, 192f->226f came out 306->491s against the original sweep's 288->573s, on a box showing 10-21% run-to-run variance. Real cost is a smooth ~frames^1.4. The clip ceiling is now 15.08s (362f); the pacing divisor deliberately stays UNDER it at 8 so sections default short and only speech-heavy ones grow. The historical reasoning below is kept because the REGRESSIONS it describes were real.]
config._comment_audio_speech_without_words: v0.6.0 fixes GARBLED AUDIO, confirmed by controlled A/B. Cause: prose that describes SPEAKING while supplying no words. H3 builds its audio track from this text, so telling it a woman speaks with a trembling voice and giving it no <d> line makes it synthesise a voice saying nothing -- voice-shaped noise that sounds like a corrupted file. It is silent at authoring time: the JSON validates and the render succeeds. Measured on unseeing_role scene_9, which asserted speech THREE times ('She speaks with a measured, trembling breath, her voice carrying the weight...', 'as she delivers her lines', 'The sound of her voice cracks slightly with emotion') with spokenLines:[] and zero <d> tags. Re-rendering the same scene at the same seed/geometry/model/steps with the line supplied produced clean intelligible speech. Four render-side hypotheses were falsified first and all failed IDENTICALLY because they rendered the same text: declared-timeline mismatch (dead -- scene_9's timeline fits 8s), narration/no-dialogue (dead -- scene_5 has a line and is also garbled), the previous cache implementation (dead -- ON and OFF equally garbled), and resolution (dead -- 832x480 and 1280x720 equally garbled). Incidental finding from that A/B: That previous cache implementation saved only 4s per clip at 480p (81s vs 85s), so it is near-worthless here and carries quality risk for nothing -- the 720p measurement that justified it does not transfer. THE FIX: the template now states that prose may describe speech ONLY when the words appear in a <d> tag; an empty spokenLines means nobody speaks and the prose must use breath/movement/stillness instead; background voices (a crowd, photographers, a name called) must either get a line or be described non-vocally; overallSoundscape carries NO voice at all, not even abstractly, since the official guide reserves it for non-verbal sound; and a speaker's vocal identity (age, register, pace, accent) goes OUTSIDE the tag on first appearance. Terminal check 0a asks the model to find every speech verb and confirm each has words attached. NOTE the repair script artifacts/h3-prompt-compliance/strip_borrowed_dialogue.mjs CREATED this defect on scene_9 by deleting a borrowed <d> and leaving the speech prose; it now detects and reports the condition instead of shipping it silently.
config._comment_scoped_section: v0.18.0: scene_detail is wired scope:'matching' and the PROMPT interpolates only that fragment, never the whole scenes_plan. Cross-section dialogue/entity leakage (issue #3) was not a prompt-following failure that could be fixed by asking harder -- it was the node being handed every other section's lines and entities and told to filter. Measured live on ember_wright: scene_1 (allowlist vashti_oru, the_rift_forge, the_last_ember) authored the_courier + iron_lantern and all THREE of the film's spoken lines, duplicating scenes 2 and 3, and was rejected by the render-side reference gate. scenes_plan stays declared because it is the itemSource the walker fans out over, but it is no longer visible to the model.
config._comment_continuity_chain: v0.25.0 CLOSES THE HANDOFF CHAIN. `continuationAnchor` existed since the structured rewrite and described each scene's end state 'so a later scene can continue cleanly' -- and NOTHING READ IT. scene_video_prompt's inputs were this scene's own scene_detail plus the bibles, so every scene was authored blind to its predecessor's realised end state. That is the single root cause of three defects the founder caught by watching (a character present instead of arriving, a fixture moving between cuts, a beat skipped so people teleported) and one found by reading the prompts against each other: scene 1 ended with the tea poured and steaming while scene 2 opened asserting the cups were not yet visible. The fix is the self-edge above -- scope:'previousN', n:1, the SAME mechanism chapter_screenplay_draft already uses -- which exposes the immediately preceding scene's finished prompt as {{scene_video_prompt}}. The author copies its continuationAnchor into continuationFrom and opens on it. concurrency is 1 because scene N's call depends on scene N-1's completed output; the engine force-clamps any node with a previousN input to serial anyway, so this is documentation of a constraint rather than a knob. COST: scene prompts no longer author in parallel. That is the price of the chain and it is worth it -- the authoring calls are cheap next to a 119s render per clip. Both fields are STRUCTURED LEDGERS, not prose, because prose rules in this bundle have drifted twice; the runner (dhee-runner-minimax-h3 >=0.6.0) compiles continuationFrom into directed prose before [Shot 1] and no longer emits continuationAnchor at all -- it describes a state after the clip ends.
config._comment_scoped_ids: v0.31.0: back to the built-in llm.generate, now that dhee-core owns per-item enum binding (cfg.perItemEnums). v0.30.0 routed this node through an EXTERNAL llm.generate_scoped runner because cfg.outputSchema is one static path resolved once against bundleDir -- every item of a collection fan-out got a byte-identical schema, so the model was free to write an id belonging to a different section, and the mismatch was only caught downstream at render ('unknown references[2].id="chocolate_bar"') after GPU time was already spent. That external runner worked (zero repairs across 6 scenes on thinkingcap-27b) but it had to reimplement ~40% of llm.generate -- template substitution, the retry loop, pendingCritiques, skip-if-exists -- and lost CAS, purely to own the call. The hole was never bundle-specific: it is llm.generate's own structured-output contract over COLLECTIONS, so the fix belongs in the engine. perItemEnums injects this section's entities[] as an enum into a COPY of the schema (GBNF-compiled on the local gateway, so a stray id is UNDECODABLE), re-checks every id after the call, and feeds violations into the same retry loop that already self-corrects schema failures. characterPaths/sceneryPaths additionally catch an id that is licensed but in the WRONG SLOT -- a character in sceneryIds is fatal at render and no enum can prevent it (measured on ashfall_crown scene_3: ash_sworn_riders). enumSchemaPaths still OMITS dialogue subjectId (an offScreen speaker legitimately has no plate, and a grammar cannot express the exemption -- it is CHECKED instead) and both continuation ledgers (a boundary ledger is the previous scene's end state, not this scene's cast).

nodes.displayName: Scene Clips (MiniMax H3 multi-cut reference-to-video, up to 15s, native AV)

config._comment: One H3 call per SECTION. shotPlanInput lets the runner sum the section's shot durations into the clip length when the authored prompt does not state one; statePlanInput/stateImagesInput give the same per-state plate substitution comfy.ltx_msr does, merged across the section's shots (last state wins) because one render can only hold one plate per character. maxRefs is 9, H3's real limit, against MSR's 5. scheduler is the founder-tested 'simple' recipe. 1344x768 is H3's native geometry (768 short edge, capped 768x1344, /32). SHEET SPLIT (sheetPanels 4): character_anchor_image and character_state_image are 4-panel multi-view identity SHEETS (1536x864, four 384x864 panels: front full-body, profile, three-quarter, medium close-up) built for LTX MSR. H3 reads a reference as a literal photograph, so handed the sheet it RENDERS IT INTO THE FRAME as several people against a backdrop -- measured in dhee-cofounder/artifacts/h3-r2v-probe cell A, where the bottom ~40% of every frame is a reproduction of the sheet. So the runner crops each sheet and sends panels [0, 3] -- the full-body view and the close-up -- as SEPARATE references, which is what H3's 9 slots exist for. viewsPerCharacter walks down to 1 automatically when a crowded scene would overflow. Do NOT set sheetPanels to 0 here without changing the anchor stage to emit single views. RESOLUTION IS A DELIBERATE COST DECISION (founder call, 2026-08-03): 1344x768 is H3's NATIVE geometry (768 short edge, capped 768x1344) and 2.58x the pixels of the stock ComfyUI template, which sets width/height from a ResolutionSelector at 0.4 megapixels (~832x480). Measured on the 5090: a 5s/124-frame clip is 178s at 1344x768 vs 68s at the template's 0.4MP, and a 15s/362-frame scene runs ~42 s/it, i.e. ~18-20 min, making a 10-section film roughly a 3-hour render. That is accepted, not an oversight: at 480p a full-body character resolves the face to too few pixels and the identity plates stop doing their job. Lower width/height per project if you are iterating on prompts rather than rendering a final cut. CANONICAL FAST H3 GRAPH (founder-tested on the 5090, 2026-08-05): workflows/minimax_h3_r2v.json uses minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot, PathchSageAttentionKJ(auto), MiniMaxH3Cache (threshold 0.03, active 15%-90%, max_steps 1), res_multistep, and the simple scheduler. These config values intentionally mirror the workflow because the runner accepts per-call overrides. Set cache:false to A/B cache quality while retaining the runner's safe model rewiring.
config._comment_duration_cap: v0.9.0: CLIP_CAP raised 8 -> 10s at the founder's request, and propagated to every place that encodes it (chapter_outline divisor, secondsPerShot 5, scene_detail shot max, scene_video_prompt duration max). COST WARNING, measured: a duration sweep at 720p found H3's marginal cost jumps ~3.5x between 8.00s (192 frames, 288s) and 9.42s (226 frames, 573s). 10s snaps to 243 frames (10.13s), which is PAST that knee, so a clip costs roughly 2x an 8s one under the cache settings measured at that time. 8.00s remains the cheapest point per second of finished video; 10s is a deliberate quality/pacing choice, not an efficiency one. [CORRECTED v0.13.0: the '~3.5x marginal cost jump between 8.00s and 9.42s' cited here is RETRACTED as measurement noise -- re-measured with fixed steps, 192f->226f came out 306->491s against the original sweep's 288->573s, on a box showing 10-21% run-to-run variance. Real cost is a smooth ~frames^1.4. The clip ceiling is now 15.08s (362f); the pacing divisor deliberately stays UNDER it at 8 so sections default short and only speech-heavy ones grow. The historical reasoning below is kept because the REGRESSIONS it describes were real.]

pinnedRefs.appearsAs: the real primary location, exactly as photographed
pinnedRefs.job: the location, its architecture, surfaces, set dressing and the quality of its light

config._comment_pinned_operator_photos: v0.7.0 lets an operator hand the bundle REAL photographs. Previously every plate was generated (comfy.tti anchors from the story bible), and there was no way to say 'the lead looks like THIS person'. referenceInputs could not express it either: it resolves the prompt's own references[] by id, so a plate only reaches a clip if the AUTHORING MODEL cites it -- and the model has no way to know an operator input exists. pinnedRefs bypasses references[] and attaches the photo to EVERY clip, which is the right semantics: 'use this actress's face' is a constraint on the whole film, not a per-scene creative decision. Pinned plates are PREPENDED before routeRefs, and that ordering is what makes them OVERRIDE rather than merely add -- routeRefs dedupes by path, keeps only the FIRST background (so location_photo displaces the generated location plate) and fills subject slots in order (so protagonist_photo takes the lowest <Subject N> number and survives the maxRefs cap). Both inputs are OPTIONAL: unsupplied means 'use the generated anchors', and an unreadable file is skipped with a note rather than failing the run. Note the interaction with sheetPanels: generated character plates are multi-view SHEETS that get split into single views, whereas an operator photo is already a single view and passes through untouched. v0.7.1 BUGFIX: both inputs shipped in v0.7.0 WITHOUT a `path` field, which broke every run of this bundle -- walker.ts resolves a kind:'file' input with resolve(projectDir, d.path), so an absent path threw 'The paths[1] argument must be of type string. Received undefined' before any node executed. `required:false` does NOT make `path` optional: the walker needs a path to test existsSync against, and only THEN does required:false let it skip a missing file. So an optional file input still declares where the file would live.

config._comment_reroll: seed is the BASE; the runner uses (seed + hash(itemId)) so each scene differs but is reproducible. To re-roll ONE bad clip today you must bump this base, which shifts every scene's lineage — a poor mechanism. A per-project `seed` field (same pattern as render_steps/resolution) would make it a one-line project change instead.
config._comment_v0_27_0_protagonist_photo_remov: v0.27.0 REMOVED protagonist_photo. It and the cast-photo slots were two ways to do the same thing and the operator could not tell them apart. The slots win: they SKIP plate generation (comfy.tti copies the photo instead of calling Comfy) and they work for any number of characters, matched by name. protagonist_photo was a pinnedRef -- it attached one face to EVERY clip whether or not that character was in the scene, and still paid to generate the plate it then displaced. location_photo is kept: it is the only way to pin a real PLACE, has no cast-slot equivalent, and a single background per clip is exactly the right semantics for it.

Measured on the first desktop run: a real photo of Meera arrived beside 'pale complexion, oval face, long black hair pulled back loosely, simple white cotton kurta'. The runner (>=0.6.5) rewrites appearsAs for any character matching a cast-photo name to defer to the image. `job` is untouched -- it names which FEATURES to follow, which is still what we want.

config._comment_no_upscale: v0.14.0: concatenates scene_clip DIRECTLY -- the scene_upscaled pass was removed. Measured against ground truth (a real 1280x720 photoreal clip degraded 4x and upscaled back, scored against the original), comfy.ltx_upscale LOST to a free ffmpeg lanczos upscale on H3 output on BOTH fidelity (Y-SSIM 0.9193 vs 0.9634) and detail (edge energy 86.7% vs 90.4% of truth): its output was softer than its own input. Feeding H3's own generation prompt verbatim changed nothing (83.3% vs 83.9%), so it was not a conditioning problem. H3 output is also intrinsically soft -- a 4x downscale of it destroyed only 10% of its edge energy, so there is little detail for any upscaler to recover. The whole render-cheap-finish-sharp premise does not hold for this generator, and the earlier claim that H3 cost scales as pixels^1.3 (true for RESOLUTION) was being used to justify a quality trade it does not buy. If a larger delivery size is needed, scale with ffmpeg after the concat -- it is free and measurably more faithful. See dhee-cofounder/memory/2026-08-04-ltx-upscale-loses-to-lanczos-on-h3-output.md.

_comment_v0_14_0: Upscale pass REMOVED entirely (founder directive). v0.12.0 had swapped comfy.rtx_vsr -> comfy.ltx_upscale on the premise that a generative refine could rebuild detail a cheap render lost; a ground-truth test the same day falsified it -- comfy.ltx_upscale is measurably WORSE than a free ffmpeg lanczos upscale on H3 output, softer than its own input, and unaffected by prompt conditioning. See final_video._comment_no_upscale. Consequences: final_video concatenates scene_clip directly, the comfy.ltx_upscale runner dep and the `upscale` project field are gone, and the bundle is 30 nodes. The `resolution` field still governs H3's own render size, which is where the real quality/cost lever is (480p 55s vs 720p 154s vs 768p 205s at 124 frames -- a 3.7x spread). Render at the resolution you intend to deliver; there is no sharpening pass to lean on.
_comment_v0_15_0:
chapter_screenplay now performs real ADAPTATION rather than transcription. The pass previously asked the director to "compress ruthlessly" and framed the job as "what a viewer standing in the room would see and hear" -- which points at filming the paragraphs in order. But prose is mostly interiority, backstory, description and summary, and a viewer in the room sees NONE of that, so the hardest and most common adaptation problem (a paragraph of someone thinking) had no instruction at all: it got dropped and the chapter's meaning went with it. Selection was also BINARY (written as a beat, or silently gone) and UNRECORDED, so nothing downstream could tell a deliberate omission from an oversight.

New required  section: every meaningful element of the chapter gets exactly one row with a disposition -- DRAMATISE (becomes a beat) / DIALOGUE / SETTING / SOUND / IMPLY (the cut carries it) / CUT (with a reason). Only DRAMATISE rows become beats, one-to-one and in order, each headed . Interiority may NEVER be DRAMATISE. Four consequences: the director gets the craft vocabulary the prompt was missing; interiority must land somewhere instead of evaporating; omissions become auditable (CUT + reason) so no later stage helpfully re-adds them; and THE SECONDS BUDGET NOW BITES AT SELECTION TIME (~durationSec/8 DRAMATISE rows) instead of being asserted upstream and then enforced by a downstream clamp with no judgement -- the v0.8.1 failure where a 35-section film came out 4m34s against a 6m34s plan. SOUND is called out as the under-used lever: H3 generates synced audio from the same prompt, so conveying something by sound is free.

Terminal self-check added (this bundle has measured that the terminal position holds best), verifying row coverage, the DRAMATISE count against budget, beat<->row correspondence, that no DRAMATISE row is interiority, that every non-DRAMATISE row names a beat that really carries it, and that every CUT has a reason.

Prompt-only change -- chapter_screenplay emits markdown and has no outputSchema. NOT YET RUN. The design discussion also identified a follow-on: with the disposition table in place, "did we lose the story?" becomes a checkable question and a coverage-critic pass has something concrete to check against. That is deliberately NOT built yet -- note that bundles_removed_no_direction_planning/ holds two agentic bundles that were pulled for lacking direction planning, i.e. agency without a plan to work against. Dispositions first, critic second.
_comment_v0_16_0: Coverage critic added, closing the loop v0.15.0's Adaptation table opened. chapter_screenplay_draft authors the adaptation (unchanged prompt); the new chapter_screenplay re-reads the SOURCE PROSE against the draft's disposition table and fixes only what fell through -- unaccounted elements, interiority wrongly marked DRAMATISE, dispositions that land in no beat, unjustified CUTs, broken table<->beat correspondence. It MUST NOT touch beats, so continuity stays valid and it cannot drift into re-authoring; a clean draft passes through verbatim with a `### Coverage Audit` note. Naming is deliberate: the reviewed node keeps the `chapter_screenplay` id so all three downstream consumers and both {{chapter_screenplay}} template variables keep working -- llm.generate derives template vars from input ids, so repointing consumers would have broken chapter_outline.md and chapter_state.md silently. 30 -> 31 nodes; the reduction to pay for it is the chapter_outline collapse (a deterministic split of the now-labelled `#### Beat N` headings), which is planned and not yet built.
_comment_v0_17_0: schemas/scene_outline.schema.json now DECLARES speechOverflowSec. plan.chapter_merge writes that field (chapterMerge.ts:499) on any section whose dialogue needs more time than the clip ceiling, but the schema was additionalProperties:false and did not list it -- so the merge wrote a field its own output schema forbade and the whole run died with "/sections/N must NOT have additional properties". REPRODUCED against a real 46-section project: under the old 10.83s ceiling exactly sections [7,9,11,12,23,31,32,33,36,37] overflowed, character-for-character the reported error. It only bites DIALOGUE-HEAVY films -- a section that never overflows never gets the field, which is why a 7-section test story with 4 short lines passed and a 46-section talky one failed. That was a hole in test coverage, not a property of how the run was launched. Paired with the dhee-runner-story-chapters fix raising H3_GRID_CEILING_FRAMES 260 -> 362, overflow on that project drops from 10 sections to 2, and the 2 that remain are now legal.
_comment_v0_18_0_no_upscale: The upscale pass is GONE and its dependency declarations are removed with it. The graph ends scene_clip -> final_video (ffmpeg.concat). The node itself had already been dropped, but dependencies.runners/runnerPackages still declared comfy.ltx_upscale, so every install of this bundle pulled a runner nothing used and the v0.12.0/v0.14.0 comments still described a stage that does not run. Founder call 2026-08-08: the pass is not worth its cost here -- H3 already renders at its native 1344x768 (the resolution input's 'native'), so a generative re-upscale spends GPU re-synthesising pixels that were never downsampled. _comment_v0_23_0_krea2_plates: Anchor plates move from Z-Image to KREA2 (founder call 2026-08-08: Krea2 produces better characters, especially dark-fantasy ones). Measured head-to-head on a single hard prompt — a hooded figure whose robe frays into hundreds of individual root tendrils, face held in shadow — same seed, same 832x1216 geometry: krea2_turbo_fp8 at 8 steps vs zit_turbo_stableyogi at 9. Krea2 is ~2.5x slower per plate (16.1s vs 6.5s at 1MP) and that is accepted: a plate is generated once per character and then reused by every shot in the film, so identity quality is worth far more here than generation speed. ALL THREE anchor nodes moved together, not just characters — plates from two different models do not share a look, and H3 receives them side by side as references for the same frame. NOTE a step sweep found more sampling does NOT buy detail on either model (Z-Image scored LOWER at 28 steps than at 9), so the plate quality ceiling is the model, not the schedule.
